h: The Torah Is Near Even in the Lowliest Soul

p: כִּי הַמִּצְוָה הַזֹּאת וְגוֹמֵר (דְּבָרִים ל, יא–יג)
"It is not in heaven, that you should say,
'Who will go up to heaven for us
and bring it to us,'" etc.;
"nor is it across the sea, that you should say,
מִי יַעֲבָר לָנוּ אֶל עֵבֶר הַיָּם
'Who will cross to the other side of the sea for us.'"
And Rashi, of blessed memory, explained:
you would have to go up after it."
And they derived this from the superfluous language
"that you should say, 'Who will go up for us,'" etc.,
"that you should say, 'Who will cross for us'";
for it would have sufficed to say,
and "nor is it across the sea."
And from the implication of the word "that you should say,"
it appears that one would have needed
that one would need to go up to heaven
if the Torah is not found here,
or the teacher to teach him Torah,
one is obligated to seek after it.
But in heaven there is no such possibility,
as is known from the halachos that were forgotten,
שֶׁהוּא עַל פִּי מַאֲמַר הַגְּמָרָא שָׁם (עֵרוּבִין נה, א)
that it follows the statement of the Gemara there (Eruvin 55a)
that the Torah will not be found
in one who raises his mind up to the heavens;
and "nor is it across the sea":
that it will not be found
with one who broadens his mind like the sea.
rather of one who truly has
an elevated heart in the ways of Hashem,
to be lifted in his soul
עַל כׇּל עִנְיְנֵי חֶמְדַּת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה
above all matters of the delights of this world,
and he "rides upon the heights of the earth,"
and his soul is always bound to heaven.
וּכְמוֹ כֵן מִי שֶׁלִּבּוֹ רָחָב כַּיָּם
And likewise one whose heart is broad like the sea,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ רוֹחַב לֵב בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה
that is, who has breadth of heart in words of Torah,
whose heart is full of words of Torah,
some self-elevation and superiority in his soul
he has no connection in essence
for the words of Torah to be acquired by him;
for words of Torah are likened to water,
which descend from a high place
"that you should say, 'Who will go up to heaven for us
that is, in truth there is need
above all the delights of this world,
אִם הָרַב דּוֹמֶה לְמַלְאַךְ ה׳ צְבָאוֹת
"If the teacher resembles an angel of Hashem of Hosts,
they should seek Torah from his mouth."
And this is "Who will go up for us," etc.,
that is, that we learn words of Torah from him.
וְכֵן מִי יַעֲבוֹר לָנוּ אֶל עֵבֶר הַיָּם
And likewise "Who will cross to the other side of the sea for us
that is, so precious a soul,
whose heart is full of words of Torah.
And the truth is that this is needed,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסוֹף הוֹרָיוֹת (הוֹרָיוֹת יג, ב)
as written at the end of Horayos (Horayos 13b):
one who can declare all His praise."
וּכְדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִפּוֹל לֵב הָאָדָם עָלָיו מִזֶּה
And so that a person's heart not fall within him over this,
when he sees and feels in himself
that he has a lowly soul,
that it is not in his power to reach
and he also has no such teacher
from whom he can learn and receive;
he should not despair of himself;
For in truth words of Torah
כִּי קָרוֹב אֵלֶיךָ הַדָּבָר מְאוֹד (שָׁם, יד)
"For the matter is very near to you" (Devarim 30:14),
"in your mouth and in your heart," specifically,
each one according to what he is.
וְעַל כֵּן אָמַר זֶה לְשׁוֹן יָחִיד
And therefore it said this in the singular,
although it opened in the plural,
"for us," "and make us hear it," "that we may do it";
that since the Merciful One desires the heart,
גַּם אִם יֵשׁ לוֹ נֶפֶשׁ נְמוּכָה מְאוֹד
even if he has a very lowly soul,
to do the service incumbent upon him
according to his strength and intellect,
he will be praised by his mouth,
and he is very precious before Him, may He be blessed.
to Rabbi Chaim Vital, of blessed memory,
שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ נְשָׁמָה גָּבוֹהַּ מְאוֹד יוֹתֵר מִמֶּנּוּ
who had a soul far higher than his,
וְעִם כׇּל זֶה הוּא יוֹתֵר חָשׁוּב
and nonetheless he is more precious
through his service according to his level
before Him, may He be blessed.
וְגַם אִם יְהֵא נִצְרָךְ לְרַב כָּזֶה
And also, if he will need such a teacher,
Hashem Yisbarach will certainly provide him
with David HaMelech, peace be upon him,
as is known from the Arizal;
וְכֵן אָמַר בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (מִדְרָשׁ תְּהִלִּים טז, יא)
and so it says in the Midrash (Midrash Tehillim 16:11)
"I would rather stand at the threshold in the house of my God":
Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov in the inner chamber,
Moshe and Aharon in the hall,
And precisely in such a lowly station
he accomplished before Him, may He be blessed, wondrously,
and did not want this soul,
but in truth he will be at the head,
"He will be exalted and lifted up," etc.,
and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, expounded:
and more than Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him.
כִּי קָרוֹב אֵלֶיךָ הַדָּבָר מְאֹד בְּפִיךָ
"For the matter is very near to you, in your mouth":
he is very precious before Him, may He be blessed,
"A prayer of the poor man when he enwraps himself";
שֶׁהוּא עוֹטֵף אֶת כׇּל הַתְּפִלּוֹת שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם
for he envelops all the prayers in the world,
because his prayer is accepted before Him, may He be blessed.
As we find with Menasheh, king of Yehudah,
as having no share in the World to Come;
and nonetheless they expounded about him
"He turned to the prayer of the destitute
וְלֹא בָזָה אֶת תְּפִלָּתָם (תְּהִלִּים קב, יח)
and did not despise their prayer" (Tehillim 102:18).
And they also expounded this (in Midrash Rabbah, Emor)
which is destitute of good deeds,
and we have nothing on which to lean,
and nothing is left us but prayer;
וְעִם כׇּל זֶה לֹא בָזָה אֶת תְּפִלָּתָם
and nonetheless "He did not despise their prayer";
for every individual soul of Yisrael,
its prayer is accepted before Him, may He be blessed,
to be saved in all its affairs.

Each Soul Can Serve From Its Place
The Poor Soul’s Prayer Reaches Hashem
